name: Wire-Tech
old_description: Wire Tech has been making components for handgun and rifles since 1996. What constitutes a good firearm? We agree with most owners who say a firearm that is manufactured with quality workmanship would produce the one needed ingredient: reliability. This is something that WireTech strides to achieve with every job, customer and commitment.
about:
Wire Tech LLC operates from Watertown, Connecticut, where it was founded in 1996. The company began by producing components for handguns and rifles, establishing a focus on precision machining for firearms.

The shop specializes in wire EDM, sinker EDM, and fast-hole EDM drilling, supported by CNC milling and a full tool room. Its equipment roster includes multiple Mitsubishi wire EDMs (FX10, FA-V, FX20K, FA-10V), a Sodick ALN600G, a Mitsubishi MV1200R, an EX-8 sinker EDM, and a CNC Ct300 fast-hole driller. The facility handles prototype through production volumes, with programming performed by experienced tool and die makers using ESPRIT CAD/CAM software.

Wire Tech serves the medical, firearms, aerospace, automotive, electronics, instrumentation, and molding industries. It has supplied firearm components since 1996 and performs sub-contract work for automotive, aircraft, and small-arms manufacturers. Medical production jobs run alongside tooling and prototype work without workflow interruption.

The company emphasizes that its programming and setups are done by diemakers who understand part function and clearances, allowing computerized operations to catch deviations early. It offers 24-hour emergency service, retains all job data for exact repeat orders, and maintains ISO 9001:2015 certification with inspection capabilities including optical contour projection, hardness testing, and calibrated gauging.

name: Wisconsin Metal Parts
old_description: Since 1988, we have provided high-quality manufacturing solutions for companies across the country
about:
Wisconsin Metal Parts operates from Waukesha, Wisconsin. The company was founded in 1988 as Die Concepts, Inc. and renamed Wisconsin Metal Parts in 2010 to reflect its expanded services. In 2024, it was acquired by SOLV Metals, joining a larger group of metal manufacturers while retaining its management team and skilled workforce.

The shop provides integrated metal fabrication, CNC machining, wire EDM, metal stamping, tool and die making, and assembly services under one roof. Its fabrication equipment includes fiber laser cutting, CNC punching, CNC bending, CNC forming, welding, and hardware insertion. Wire EDM handles electrically conductive materials up to 16 inches thick, with dedicated carbide-cutting capacity running 24/7. CNC turning offers bar feeding to 3-inch diameter, a 25.6-inch swing, and parts up to 40 inches long by 14.3 inches in diameter. Stamping presses run up to .188-inch thick, specializing in high-volume, tight-tolerance work from .003 to .060 inch thick, producing nearly 60 million stampings annually at a 98% on-time delivery rate.

Customers span aerospace, agriculture, foodservice, medical, military/defense, and the container industry. The company handles projects ranging from military ordnance mechanical fuzes and shell casing machining to steel detent plates and stainless steel dispensing nozzles, serving both prototype and production quantities across low-to-high volume, high-mix runs.

Wisconsin Metal Parts emphasizes intellectual value and the "Golden Rule" in its mission: minimizing risk, delivering high-value solutions, and building trust through open communication. Its cross-trained workforce maintains workflow flexibility, while in-house tool design uses forming and stamping simulation software to validate designs before die construction.

old_description: Wisconsin Steel Fabrication LLC is a steel fabrication and manufacturing company in Omro, Wisconsin. We handle everything from large modular and  construction projects all the way down to small repair work and support members for residential projects. We are a family business run by two brothers born and raised in Berlin WI. Since our inception in a small 900 sq ft, back yard garage with just a few welders, and a small forklift, we have proven that no job is too big or too small for us to be able to tackle. We now have grown to a 12 acre, 25,000 square ft facility with cutting edge equipment and experienced staff. We pride ourselves on Quality and on time delivery. about:
Wisconsin Steel Fabrication LLC operates from Omro, Wisconsin, where it began as a family venture started by two brothers raised in nearby Berlin. The company traces its roots to a 900-square-foot backyard garage equipped with a handful of welders and a small forklift, growing from that modest start into a 12-acre campus encompassing 25,000 square feet of production space.

The shop provides steel fabrication and manufacturing services spanning large modular fabrication, small modular fabrication, structural steel, custom fabrication, railings and stairs, and certified welding. Its capabilities cover projects ranging from sizable modular and construction builds down to repair work and support members for residential jobs, all executed within the expanded facility.

Customers come from the construction sector, modular building projects, and residential markets, with the company positioning itself to handle both large-scale commercial modules and smaller residential repair tasks.

The founders emphasize quality and on-time delivery as core differentiators, stating that customer satisfaction drives the business and that they will find a way to make any project or idea happen.

name: Wisconsin Wire Works, Inc.
old_description: Wisconsin Wire Works Inc. is an integrated manufacturer of copper and copper alloy welding wire. Five copper-industry veterans founded our company in 1994, and in a relatively short time, we've built an enviable reputation as a reliable supplier of top-quality, made-in-the-USA welding products. Today, our customers can be found on every continent.
about:
Wisconsin Wire Works, Inc. was founded in 1994 in Wales, Wisconsin, by five copper-industry veterans who set out to produce copper and copper alloy welding wire. The company remains privately held, with John Turriff serving as president and owner alongside vice presidents Tressa Turriff and Ryan Turriff.

The firm operates as an integrated manufacturer of welding consumables, drawing wire from base stocks sourced from established suppliers. Its facilities house state-of-the-art drawing equipment and an in-house welding laboratory staffed by welding engineers, metallurgists, and fabrication specialists. Products include aluminum bronze, silicon bronze, deoxidized copper, phosphor bronze, copper alloy brazing wires, and nickel aluminum bronze, supplied in precision layer-level wound spools, straightened-and-cut lengths, reels, coils, and barrel packs. All wire undergoes thorough inspection for size, cleanliness, cast, and helix before shipment.

The company serves welders, fabricators, and manufacturers across industries that rely on automatic and robotic welding, with customers on every continent. Its ABS certification also positions it as a supplier to marine and offshore sectors.

Wisconsin Wire Works emphasizes customer-driven quality: drawing dies are reworked on a fixed schedule rather than only when worn, non-contaminating lubricants are used exclusively, and products are cleaned and packed in hermetic moisture-barrier cartons. The quality system is certified to ISO 9001:2000, and the company highlights its made-in-the-USA origin as a core differentiator.

name: Wise Plastics
old_description: 100+ presses from 35 to 1100 tons, liquid silicone molding, and value-added operations under one quality system — 30 minutes from Chicago and O'Hare.
about:
Wise Plastics Technologies, headquartered in St. Charles, Illinois, traces its roots to 1974 when it was founded as Wise‑Hamlin Plastics in the greater Chicagoland area. The company has remained independently owned and operates three purpose‑built facilities totaling more than 350,000 square feet, all within 30 minutes of Chicago and O’Hare International Airport.

The molder runs over 100 injection presses ranging from 35 to 1,100 tons, supporting custom plastic injection molding, two‑shot, insert and over‑molding, in‑mold labeling, and liquid silicone rubber (LSR) molding for medical‑grade and biocompatible applications. Value‑added operations include assembly, sonic welding, heat staking, printing, decorating, packaging and kitting. Engineering services cover design for manufacturing, rapid prototyping, mold design and build, process optimization and failure analysis. The quality lab provides first‑article inspection, capability studies, IQ/OQ/PQ, PPAP and CMM inspection, with scientific molding processes monitored 24/5 and 24/7 when demand requires.

Wise Plastics serves the medical device and pharmaceutical sectors, holding ISO 13485:2016 certification for medical‑device quality management, and is ITAR registered for defense‑related work. The company also supports a range of other industries through its supply‑chain management, inventory and logistics programs.

Founded on a vision to provide reliable, high‑quality injection molding partnerships, Wise Plastics emphasizes purpose‑built facilities, integrated manufacturing operations, advanced automation on every cell, and a team of 200‑plus skilled employees who operate around the clock. Its quality system is certified to ISO 9001:2015 and ISO 13485:2016, and the firm holds OSHA SHARP recognition for safety.

name: WishBone Medical, Inc.
old_description: WishBone Medical is a Warsaw, IN, based pediatric orthopedic company focused globally on the unmet needs of children suffering from orthopedic issues. Our mission is to provide anatomically appropriate solutions in single-use, sterile packed procedure kits to surgeons and their patients who are still growing.
about:
WishBone Medical, Inc. is a pediatric orthopedic company based in Warsaw, Indiana. The company focuses on the unmet needs of children suffering from orthopedic issues, aiming to provide anatomically appropriate solutions for growing patients.

The company designs and manufactures anatomically appropriate implants and instruments, delivered in single-use, sterile-packed procedure kits. Its product lines include growth control systems, plating systems, and bone void fillers. Kits are assembled with multi-barrier sterile packaging and include web-based software for precise correction in all planes. All instruments are supplied sharp and pristine for each procedure, eliminating the need for loaner trays and reducing operating room turnover time.

WishBone Medical serves pediatric orthopedic surgeons and hospitals, providing kits that streamline procedural efficiency and reduce overall patient care costs. Its customers include medical facilities that perform pediatric orthopedic surgeries.

The company was founded to address the lack of anatomically appropriate solutions for growing patients. Its single-use kit model aims to reduce infection risk, eliminate set processing, and decrease hospital setup and processing time, enabling more children to receive proper treatment each day.

old_description: Wolf Metals has been at the forefront of custom metal fabrication in Ohio for over three decades. Founded in 1974 by Jim and Mike Wolf, our family-owned company has grown from a small local shop to a leading metal fabrication expert serving industries across the United States.
about:
Wolf Metals operates from Columbus, Ohio, where it was founded in 1974 by Jim and Mike Wolf. The family-owned business began as a small local shop and has grown into a custom metal fabrication specialist serving customers nationwide.

The company provides a full range of fabrication services including laser cutting, water jet cutting, forming, shearing, MIG and TIG welding, fastener insertion, powder coating, plating, assembly, CNC machining, leveling, tube laser cutting, laser welding, and aluminum composite material (ACM) panel fabrication. Its 100,000-square-foot facility houses more than 50 state-of-the-art machines, enabling production runs from single prototypes to high-volume orders.

Wolf Metals serves the automotive, aerospace, defense, energy, medical, agriculture, construction, and industrial machinery sectors. A recent project involved engineering a modular aluminum exoskeleton for DTi Creative to transform John Deere Gators into performance vehicles for marching bands.

The company emphasizes uncompromising quality, continuous innovation, customer focus, integrity, and teamwork as core values. It promotes end-to-end solutions under one roof, backed by a 99.8% on-time delivery rate and a defect rate below 0.1%.

name: Wolfe Custom Woodworking LLC
old_description: Wolfe Custom Woodworking LLC is a full service design, fabrication and installation shop serving the Denver Metro Area. We focus primarily on creating built-in cabinetry, shelving, and stand alone hardwood tables and casework.
about:
Wolfe Custom Woodworking LLC operates from Englewood, Colorado, serving the Denver metropolitan area. The company was founded by Daniel E. Wolfe, who has spent many years crafting fine furniture and cabinets before establishing the LLC. The business is structured as a limited liability company under Wolfe’s sole ownership.

The shop provides full-service design, fabrication, and installation of built-in cabinetry, shelving, and stand-alone hardwood tables and casework. Projects range from custom banquettes and dining tables to media credenzas, bookshelves, hutches, and side tables. Work is executed using traditional joinery techniques such as bowtie joints and hand-carved bevels, with each piece designed and fabricated by Wolfe himself. Materials include white oak, North American black walnut, Indian rosewood, and vinyl for casework applications.

The company serves residential clients throughout the Denver Metro Area seeking custom woodwork for kitchens, dining rooms, home offices, and entertainment spaces. Past projects include a white oak banquette and dining table, a walnut banquette, a mid-century modern media credenza, a solid walnut bookshelf, a shaker hutch, and a modern side table featuring a bookmatched Indian rosewood top. A client testimonial describes a custom walnut barn door for a master bathroom.

Wolfe emphasizes direct client involvement in the design process, believing that custom work should reflect each customer’s exact vision. He cites a passion for creating pieces that clients will use and love for years, and differentiates the shop by personally handling every stage of design and fabrication.

about:
Wood Components & Technologies operates from Cedar Falls, Iowa. The business evolved from a producer of wood bearings for agricultural equipment and washing machines into a manufacturer of wood and plastic OEM parts for a range of industries.

The company produces curved and arched moldings, lineal trim, and specialty millwork for commercial contractors and home builders. It also machines wood and plastic OEM components for manufacturers of machinery equipment. CNC machining is a core process used for custom millwork, including arched windows, doors, and handrails.

Its customer base includes architects, building centers, contractors, and homeowners in the commercial and residential construction sectors, as well as manufacturers of agricultural equipment and appliances. A featured project for Jokers Comedy Club in Cedar Falls highlights custom arch windows, custom doors, and machined handrail.

The firm’s focus on wood and plastic OEM parts for machinery equipment reflects a deliberate shift toward serving industrial manufacturers alongside the architectural millwork market.
